study type: Secondary data analysis of a cross-sectional study
exposure: Low maternal pre-pregnancy body mass index (PBMI) (<18.5 kg/m2)
cohort: 7,199 lactating mothers, including 284 from migrant households (where the father is an international migrant worker)
finding: Lactating mothers in migrant families had higher gestational weight gain, were more likely to be multiparous, delivered in private hospitals, and had babies with higher birth weight compared to non-migrant mothers.
mod_finding: Caesarean deliveries were positively associated with low gestational weight gain.
